title: Return-cost coupling forces N_cheap < o-e strongly enough to raise the Juggler period cutoff
statement: After a cheap OOE the next valley is at n^{9/8}. A CycleMin-legal return to n-scale has a positive letter cost, so N_cheap < o-e on every realized cycle, and the resulting finance bound excludes L=25781 at the published floor 10^6 or shrinks E_run(10^6) by a certified comparison.
counterexamples: O^{53}E^{31} from exponent 1 lands at 3^{53}/2^{84} ≈ n^{1.002}; floors O(1/x) do not pull that to n+2, so a uniform later-valley lower bound that beats n+2 enough to move the cutoff does not exist
O^{12}E^7 lands at 3^{12}/2^{19} ≈ n^{1.014} < n^{9/8}, so subsequent valleys need not sit at 9/8
At L=25781, theta ≈ 2.546e-5 versus diagnostic 9/8-charge 1.07e-4, k<=12 greedy 8.58e-5, and k<=53 walk 2.59e-5; none is a certified exclusion, and the last is still above theta
notes: The (5,3) descent and F_2(v)>v+2 on realized OOE are negative knowledge. N_sep=2324 at L=25781 is a diagnostic, not a restart-at-n theorem. Envelope walks are not leftover-killers: envelope height is an upper bound. No Paper A edit, no ledger row, no Lean. Not a halt theorem.
tested_range: Exponent search k<=53, ell<=32; OOE landings on {37,365,1999} and five starts near 10^6+53; diagnostic scan of the 99 run-type leftovers at n=10^6+1
